what_it_does: This paper presents the first complete star-by-star simulation of the Milky Way galaxy that runs on supercomputers. Simulating hundreds of billions of individual stars with realistic physics (gravity, explosions, gas dynamics) is normally impossible because supernova explosions occur at very short timescales, forcing the simulation to take tiny timesteps. The paper combines physics-based computation with machine learning prediction to skip explicit calculation of short-timescale events while maintaining accuracy.
